facts: NIOSH A–Z (hydrogen chloride) lists these 8-hour barrier materials: Butyl; Teflon; Saranex; Barricade; Responder; Trellchem; Tychem.
NIOSH A–Z (hydrogen chloride) lists these 4-hour barrier materials: Neoprene; PVC.
The hydrogen chloride entry’s skin-protection recommendation reads: “Prevent skin contact (solution) / Frostbite.”
The entry includes the warning: “Prevent possible skin freezing from direct liquid contact.”
NIOSH notes that selection recommendations are concentration‑dependent and that hydrochloric acid is referenced at 37% for the Quick Selection Guide basis.
payload.query: For hydrogen chloride, which barriers does the archived NIOSH table place in its 8-hour and 4-hour groups, and what additional hazard language appears in the entry?
payload.answer:
Evidence-grounded answer:

- NIOSH A–Z (hydrogen chloride) lists these 8-hour barrier materials: Butyl; Teflon; Saranex; Barricade; Responder; Trellchem; Tychem. [NIOSH Recommendations for Chemical Protective Clothing A-Z | NIOSH | CDC: https://archive.cdc.gov/www_cdc_gov/niosh/ncpc/azncpc.html]
- NIOSH A–Z (hydrogen chloride) lists these 4-hour barrier materials: Neoprene; PVC. [NIOSH Recommendations for Chemical Protective Clothing A-Z | NIOSH | CDC: https://archive.cdc.gov/www_cdc_gov/niosh/ncpc/azncpc.html]
- The hydrogen chloride entry’s skin-protection recommendation reads: “Prevent skin contact (solution) / Frostbite.” [NIOSH Recommendations for Chemical Protective Clothing A-Z | NIOSH | CDC: https://archive.cdc.gov/www_cdc_gov/niosh/ncpc/azncpc.html; Hazard Communication for Disinfectants Used Against Viruses | NIOSH | CDC: https://archive.cdc.gov/www_cdc_gov/niosh/topics/disinfectant/default.html]
- The entry includes the warning: “Prevent possible skin freezing from direct liquid contact.” [Hazard Communication for Disinfectants Used Against Viruses | NIOSH | CDC: https://archive.cdc.gov/www_cdc_gov/niosh/topics/disinfectant/default.html]
- NIOSH notes that selection recommendations are concentration‑dependent and that hydrochloric acid is referenced at 37% for the Quick Selection Guide basis. [Hazard Communication for Disinfectants Used Against Viruses | NIOSH | CDC: https://archive.cdc.gov/www_cdc_gov/niosh/topics/disinfectant/default.html]
